LESSON: READING 7.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why are visuals important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe visuals accompanying texts for comprehension
2. create visuals from written texts for effective communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. describe visuals accompanying texts for comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can describe visuals accompanying texts for comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. create visuals from written texts for effective communication
   In simple words: practise until you can create visuals from written texts for effective communication. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information.
4. Show that you can: describe visuals accompanying texts for comprehension

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.2.1 Reading for Information important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a text on the theme and create a visual to summarise the information in the text,
2. Work with peers in teams to conduct a pictionary session where they begin to draw a picture and another team tries to guess what it could be before it is complete,
3. Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner follows simple instructions when creating a visual to summarise the information in the text read.
4. Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner builds on their own learning experiences when describing the visuals and predicting what story or information the visual could represent. Values:
5. Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to put together a collection of varied visuals.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are visuals important?
2. How do visuals summarise information?
3. How can you help people involved in a road crash?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. describe visuals accompanying texts for comprehension
2. create visuals from written texts for effective communication

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
